question.problem:
Find the limit ${lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)\cdot g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨\frac{{t}^{2}-2t+2}{t+1},\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)}{t},\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨\frac{{e}^{2t}-1}{t},\,1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{{t}^{2}-2t+2}{t+1},\,{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)}{t},\,{lim}_{t\to 0}t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{{t}^{2}-2t+2}{t+1},\,2{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)}{(2t)},\,{lim}_{t\to 0}t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{0}^{2}-2\cdot 0+2}{0+1},\,2\cdot 1,\,0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that for the second component of ${lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)$ we used a special limit ${lim}_{u\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡u}{u}=1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{{e}^{2t}-1}{t},\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{({e}^{2t}-1)^{′}}{(t)^{′}},\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{2{e}^{2t}}{1},\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{0},\,1-\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\,0+1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,0,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that for the first component of ${lim}_{t\to 0}g(t)$ we used L'Hopital's Rule.

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)\cdot g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\  & =2\cdot 2+2\cdot 0+0\cdot 1 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
